NOTES: METHOD / CONFIDENCE
I wrote an independent base58 encoder (node + BigInt, /tmp/repr7/b58.js), verified it byte-for-byte against the reference's own --a output on 20+ UTF-8-valid inputs, then used it to synthesize --b for ARBITRARY byte arrays (including invalid-UTF-8 and NUL-containing ones that argv cannot carry). I then ran 1840 systematic cases + 250 biased-random fuzz cases (2090 total) against the reference and diffed every stdout line 2 against the model below. RESULT: 0 mismatches, 0 non-zero exit codes. The model below is exact.
Systematic coverage per byte b in 0x00..0xFF (7 shapes x 256): [b], [b,'A'], ['A',b], [0x5C,b], [b,0x5C], [b,b], [0x0A,b]. Plus full 256-byte sweeps in all four quote-presence combinations, plus targeted quote/backslash/NUL/boundary cases.

=== EXACT ALGORITHM (Python 3.12 bytes.__repr__, as printed by print(bytes)) ===

def bytes_repr(bs: list[int]) -> str:
    has_sq = 0x27 in bs
    has_dq = 0x22 in bs
    quote  = 0x22 if (has_sq and not has_dq) else 0x27      # 0x22 == '"', 0x27 == "'"
    out = "b" + chr(quote)
    for c in bs:
        if   c == 0x5C:                 out += "\\" + "\\"   # ONE backslash byte -> TWO backslash chars
        elif c == quote:                out += "\\" + chr(quote)
        elif c == 0x09:                 out += "\\t"
        elif c == 0x0A:                 out += "\\n"
        elif c == 0x0D:                 out += "\\r"
        elif c < 0x20 or c >= 0x7F:     out += "\\x%02x" % c  # LOWERCASE, always 2 digits
        else:                           out += chr(c)         # verbatim
    out += chr(quote)
    return out

The branch ORDER above is load-bearing: 0x5C is tested before the quote test (irrelevant since they differ) and before the range test (0x5C is in 0x20..0x7E, so without the early branch it would be emitted literally).

=== QUOTE-SELECTION PREDICATE (exact) ===
quote = '"'  IFF  (0x27 appears anywhere in the byte string) AND (0x22 appears nowhere in it)
quote = "'"  in all three other cases: neither present, only 0x22 present, or BOTH present.
- It is pure set membership over the WHOLE byte string. Position, order of first occurrence, distance, and counts are all irrelevant (verified: 0x27-then-0x22, 0x22-then-0x27, 20 bytes apart, doubled, tripled).
- Bytes contributed by the leading-'1' -> NUL prefix participate in the scan like any other byte (they are never 0x22/0x27, so they never change the choice).
- There is NO triple-quote fallback and no other quote character. When both 0x27 and 0x22 are present Python does NOT switch to '"' -- it stays "'" and escapes 0x27.
- Consequence, stated per byte: 0x22 is escaped NEVER (it is literal under both quotes, because quote can only be 0x22 when 0x22 is absent). 0x27 is escaped IFF 0x22 is also present in the string.

=== PARTITION OF ALL 256 BYTES (sums to 256) ===
- \\xNN lowercase, 158 bytes: 0x00-0x08, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0E-0x1F, 0x7F-0xFF.
- named escapes, 3 bytes: 0x09 -> \t, 0x0A -> \n, 0x0D -> \r.
- 0x5C -> \\ (2 chars), 1 byte.
- active quote -> backslash+quote (2 chars), 1 byte.
- literal, 93 bytes: 0x20..0x7E minus 0x5C minus the active quote char.

=== NEGATIVE RESULTS (common implementation bugs these rule out) ===
1. NO \a (0x07), \b (0x08), \v (0x0B), \f (0x0C), \0 (0x00). All are \x07/\x08/\x0b/\x0c/\x00. (verified b'\x07\x0b\x0c\x08')
2. Hex digits are LOWERCASE and zero-padded to exactly 2 (\x00, \x0b, \x7f, \xff) -- never \xB or \xFF or \x{ff}.
3. 0x7F IS escaped; 0x7E is not. Predicate is c >= 0x7F, not c > 0x7F.
4. 0x20 (space) is LITERAL. Never \x20.
5. No double-escaping / no second pass: byte pair (0x5C,0x78) prints b'\\x' and (0x5C,0x78,0x30,0x30) prints b'\\x00'. Two 0x5C -> 4 backslashes; three -> 6.
6. No run-length compression of repeated \x00 or repeated \xff.
7. Adjacent \xNN escapes are concatenated with no separator.
8. 0x85 and 0xA0 are ordinary high bytes here -> \x85, \xa0 (the rstrip whitespace set of F4 applies only to the --b INPUT string, never to the repr of the decoded bytes).

- b58decode: k leading '1' chars are stripped and re-emitted as exactly k 0x00 bytes; the remaining digits form a big integer emitted as MINIMAL big-endian bytes ((bit_length+7)//8), so the numeric part never adds its own leading 0x00.
